summary: Formats a date into a string using {year}/{month}/{date}/{hours}-style tokens.
description: Date To String takes a date on `input` (Date) — a Date object, or a date string which it converts with `new Date()` — and writes a formatted string to `currentValue` (Date String) according to `formatString` (Format). Supported tokens: {date} (day of month, 2-digit), {month} (2-digit), {monthShort} (e.g. "Jan", en-US), {year} (4-digit), {yearShort} (2-digit), {hours}, {minutes}, {seconds} (all 2-digit, 24-hour); anything else in the format passes through literally. The default format is "{year}-{month}-{date}". Each time formatting runs, `inputChanged` (Date Changed) fires; if the input is not a usable date, `currentValue` becomes an empty string and `onError` (Invalid Date) fires instead of throwing.
whenToUse: Use it to display timestamps — record creation dates, 'last saved' times — without writing code. For formats beyond these tokens (locale-aware dates, relative times like '2 h ago'), use a Function node with Intl or a date library. Note there is no {day}-of-week token.

ports.input: Date value input; also accepts a date string, converted with new Date(). An unparsable value routes to `onError`.
ports.formatString: String value with the tokens above; changing it reformats the current date immediately.
ports.currentValue: String value with the formatted result; empty string after a formatting error.
ports.inputChanged: Signal; fires each time formatting runs (new date, and reformat after a format change).
ports.onError: Signal; fires when formatting fails (e.g. invalid date), in which case `currentValue` is emptied.

patterns: A Function output producing `new Date()` on demand → `input`: timestamp an event, then show `currentValue` in a String Format sentence.
antiPatterns: Wiring a number (epoch milliseconds) to `input` — number does not cast to date; convert to a Date in a Function or Expression first.
